Definition: from the same as the first part of G2991 and the base of G5114; to quarry:--hew.
BiblicalUsage: latoméō means hew — a small word with a sharp edge. In Matthew 27:60, "which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre"; and in Mark 15:46, "and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hewn tomb matters because it was new, unused, and real — the grave that held Christ for three days was cut out of solid rock by human hands.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
